sentences.text: Welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm Emily, your host.
Today we are traveling to Lima, the capital city of Peru.
Lima is a city by the Pacific Ocean.
It is full of history, delicious food, and friendly people.
Let's explore this beautiful South American city together.
Part 2.
Where is Lima?
Lima is on the west coast of South America.
It is the largest city in Peru and also its capital.
The city sits right next to the Pacific Ocean.
It has long beaches, busy streets, and colorful neighborhoods.
Because of its location, Lima is always full of cool ocean air.
Part 3.
A short history.
Lima was founded in 1535 by the Spanish explorer Francisco Pizarro.
For many years, it was an important city for Spanish rule in South America.
Many old buildings from that time still exist today.
You can see them in the historic center of Lima, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Lima is a city where old and new meet every day.
Part 4.
What does Lima look like?
Lima is a big and busy city with more than 9 million people.
It has modern skyscrapers, old churches, and streets full of life.
Along the coast, there are cliffs with amazing views of the sea.
Many people walk or ride bikes on the paths near the beach.
The district called Miraflores is one of the most popular areas for tourists.
Part 5.
The people of Lima.
People in Lima are kind, warm, and welcoming.
They come from many different cultures.
Indigenous, Spanish, and African roots.
Most people speak Spanish, but some also speak Quechua, the old language of the Inca people.
They love to celebrate, dance, and spend time with family.
When they greet each other, they often smile and give a friendly kiss on the cheek.
Part 6.
Food in Lima.
Lima is famous for its food.
It's known as the food capital of South America.
One of the most famous dishes is ceviche.
Fresh fish cooked with lemon juice, onion, and chili.
People also enjoy Lomo Saltado, a mix of beef, rice, and potatoes.
Peruvian food uses many spices and colors.
For dessert, you can try picarones, sweet donuts, made from pumpkin, and sweet potato.
Part 7.
The ocean and nature.
The ocean is a big part of life in Lima.
People serve fish or just relax by the water.
Lima is also close to mountains and deserts.
You can take a short trip to the Andes Mountains or visit old Inca ruins near the city.
The famous Machu Picchu is in Peru too, a few hours away by train and bus.
Part 8.
Culture and art.
Lima is full of art, music, and color.
In the Barranco district, you can see street art on almost every wall.
There are museums, dance shows, and music festivals all year long.
Traditional Peruvian music uses guitars, flutes, and drums.
Very joyful and rhythmic.
At night, the city lights up with music and dance.
Part 9.
Weather in Lima.
Lima has a special kind of weather.
It almost never rains.
But the sky is often gray and cool because of the ocean air.
The best time to visit is from December to April when it's sunny and warm.
Even in winter, the temperature is comfortable and not too cold.
People say Lima has eternal spring.
It's nice all year long.
Part 10.
Daily life in Lima.
Life in Lima is lively and busy.
People go to work, take buses or taxis, and enjoy meals together after work.
Students go to school early in the morning and often wear uniforms.
Families love to spend Sundays together, eating, laughing, and watching soccer.
In the evening, people enjoy walking by the ocean to watch the sunset.
Part 11.
Special places to visit.
If you visit Lima, don't miss.
Plaza Mayor, the main square with beautiful colonial buildings.
Miraflores, modern area with ocean views.
Barranco, full of art, music, and cafes.
Huacapuclana, an ancient pyramid right in the city.
Every part of Lima tells a story.
Some old, some new.
Part 12.
Goodbye from Lima.
Thank you for joining me on this journey to Lima, Peru.
It's a city full of history, flavor, and joy.
From the ocean waves to the sound of street music, Lima is alive every day.
If you visit South America, Lima will welcome you with open arms.
Goodbye.
Or as people in Peru say, adios.
